observations: Photo 0, 1, and 2 show a used car engine lying on a concrete floor, likely in a workshop or yard.
The engine has a black plastic cover with '84.7L' and 'FORCE' printed on it, indicating a 84.7-liter displacement and possibly a brand or model name.
The engine appears dirty, with grime, oil stains, and some rust on metal parts.
A white fan is attached to the front, connected to the crankshaft pulley.
The engine block is metallic, with visible intake manifold, exhaust manifold, and various hoses and belts.
No visible damage to the block or major components, but the overall condition suggests heavy use.
The seller claims it is a 'fairly used Japanese engine' and commonly found in Toyota Tundra, Sequoia, Land...
No visible model number or VIN plate is readable in any photo.
The engine is not running; no signs of operation are visible.

claims.evidence: No visible Japanese branding or model number in any photo. The 'FORCE' label is not a known Japanese brand. The seller's claim cannot be verified from the images.

claims.claim: It is commonly found in vehicles like the Toyota Tundra, Sequoia, Land...
claims.evidence: No photo shows this clearly enough to read.

risks.risk: Engine may be damaged internally (e.g., blown head gasket, cracked block, worn bearings)
risks.proof: A video showing the engine running, or a compression test report, or a close-up of the cylinder head and block for cracks or warping.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working or severely damaged

risks.risk: Engine may have been salvaged from a wrecked or accident-damaged vehicle
risks.proof: VIN plate or vehicle history report, or a photo of the vehicle it was removed from.

risks.risk: Engine may have been modified or rebuilt with non-standard parts
risks.proof: Close-up of the oil pan, intake manifold, and cylinder head for signs of aftermarket components or repairs.

proof_requests: Video of the engine running or a compression test report.
Close-up of the engine block and cylinder head for cracks or damage.
Photo of the VIN plate or vehicle history if available.
Photo of the oil pan and intake manifold to check for aftermarket parts.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
